what: A cost model of Moonshine Tiny itself: bytes fetched and MACs per tensor group, per 4 s encoder window and per decoded token, on the measured per-dispatch traffic of ROCC_DECOUPLED.md section 8 (engine_traffic.json).

labels.measured: board counters, Lab B25 run 8 / Lab B26, copied from engine_traffic.json
labels.planned: mbxr's tile plan re-executed (the three stem convolutions), checked against B26's encoder totals
labels.derived: arithmetic here: MACs from the checkpoint's shapes; group sums; and every changed-shape number, which is the same planner on a new shape

config.note: lm_head is TIED to model.decoder.embed_tokens (no separate tensor in model.safetensors), so 9,437,184 of the checkpoint's 27,092,736 parameters -- 34.8 % -- are the one tensor the decoder re-reads whole for every token

dec_cross_attn_matmul.note: hart-0 software: q.Kc and p.Vc against the 165 cached encoder frames

dec_self_attn_matmul_per_context_token.note: hart-0 software, MACs per token ALREADY in the context; at 15 tokens the whole self-attention matmul is under 0.03 M MACs, 0.15 % of a token

decoder_token_time.source: ROCC_DECOUPLED.md section 8.9, engine with 64-byte placement, nl+ew
decoder_token_time.label: measured parts (B25 run 8) composed by decode_compose.py; SiLU and the gate multiply are estimates, as section 8.9 says

under_hardware_in_flight.stacks_note: the vocabulary prune takes bytes out of the FIXED half of a token (the weight fill, which the beams share) and the beam multiplies only the SCALING half, so the two levers work on opposite halves and stacking them is cheaper than either implies alone
